  • Trap: boundaries don't catch event-handler or async errors → put the error in state and throw during render, or throwOnError in your data library.

title: Suspense boundaries
text: A suspending component shows the nearest <Suspense fallback> until everything inside is ready. Streaming (S2E13) sends the shell then each boundary; selective hydration (S2E11). One boundary = waits for the slowest; one per component = popcorn + jumps. Group: critical first, own boundary for heavy parts, below-the-fold together. Pair each Suspense boundary with an ErrorBoundary. Trap: useEffect fetching never suspends → use use(promise) , a framework loader, or useSuspenseQuery .

title: How did it arrive?
text: HTTP is request → response: the server can't speak first. "Real-time" = the server can push the moment something happens. See it: WhatsApp Web → DevTools → Network → filter WS → click the connection → Messages . ↓ red = received, ↑ green = sent. Five transports: short polling · long polling · Server-Sent Events · WebSockets · WebRTC. Trap: "real-time means WebSockets" → no. Pick by who talks and how often (a badge can poll; AI answers stream over SSE).
html:
• HTTP is request → response: the server can't speak first. "Real-time" = the server can push the moment something happens.
  • See it: WhatsApp Web → DevTools → Network → filter WS → click the connection → Messages. ↓ red = received, ↑ green = sent.
  • Five transports: short polling · long polling · Server-Sent Events · WebSockets · WebRTC.
  • Trap: "real-time means WebSockets" → no. Pick by who talks and how often (a badge can poll; AI answers stream over SSE).

title: Short polling
text: Ask on a fixed timer ("anything new?"). Cost = latency (up to one interval) + load (10,000 tabs ÷ 5 s = 2,000 req/s, mostly empty). Fine for rare updates where seconds of delay are OK: dashboards, build status, unread badges. Works through every proxy. Trap: setInterval(fetch) overlaps when the server slows → schedule the next poll with setTimeout after the response; skip work when document.hidden .
html:
• Ask on a fixed timer ("anything new?"). Cost = latency (up to one interval) + load (10,000 tabs ÷ 5 s = 2,000 req/s, mostly empty).
  • Fine for rare updates where seconds of delay are OK: dashboards, build status, unread badges. Works through every proxy.
  • Trap: setInterval(fetch) overlaps when the server slows → schedule the next poll with setTimeout after the response; skip work when document.hidden.

title: Long polling
text: Server holds the request open until there's news (or ~30 s timeout → empty response), client immediately asks again. Near-instant, plain HTTP. Costs: full request + headers per message, one open request per user. Trap: messages in the gap between polls → send a cursor ( ?since=<last id> ) so the server returns everything after it.
html:

  • Trap: messages in the gap between polls → send a cursor (?since=<last id>) so the server returns everything after it.

title: Server-Sent Events
text: One HTTP response that never ends: Content-Type: text/event-stream . Format: id: , event: , data: lines, blank line ends an event. new EventSource('/stream') → onmessage . Auto-reconnects and sends Last-Event-ID so the server can resume. Limits: one-way (send with normal fetch POST), text only. Trap: HTTP/1.1 ≈ 6 connections per origin; each open stream holds one → 7th tab hangs. HTTP/2 multiplexes streams on one connection.
html:

  • new EventSource('/stream') → onmessage. Auto-reconnects and sends Last-Event-ID so the server can resume.
  • Limits: one-way (send with normal fetch POST), text only.
  • Trap: HTTP/1.1 ≈ 6 connections per origin; each open stream holds one → 7th tab hangs. HTTP/2 multiplexes streams on one connection.

title: WebSockets
text: Starts as HTTP GET with Upgrade: websocket → 101 Switching Protocols → same TCP connection carries frames both ways. Frame header 2–14 bytes vs hundreds of bytes of HTTP headers. wss:// = over TLS. API: onopen , send , onmessage , onclose . Each message is a task (S1E15) → batch bursts, render once per frame ( requestAnimationFrame ). Trap: WebSockets do not reconnect by themselves. Reconnect, catch up and resend are your job (E10).
html:

  • API: onopen, send, onmessage, onclose. Each message is a task (S1E15) → batch bursts, render once per frame (requestAnimationFrame).
  • Trap: WebSockets do not reconnect by themselves. Reconnect, catch up and resend are your job (E10).

title: WebRTC
text: Browser ↔ browser audio, video, data. See it: on a Meet call open chrome://webrtc-internals . Signaling (your choice, usually a WebSocket) swaps offer/answer (SDP) + ICE candidates . STUN = "what's my public address", TURN = relay when direct fails. Code: new RTCPeerConnection({ iceServers }) → createDataChannel / addTrack → createOffer → setLocalDescription → send via signaling. Trap: 100-person mesh = 99 uploads each. Big calls use an SFU (Selective Forwarding Unit): upload once, server forwards.
html:

  • Signaling (your choice, usually a WebSocket) swaps offer/answer (SDP) + ICE candidates. STUN = "what's my public address", TURN = relay when direct fails.
  • Code: new RTCPeerConnection({ iceServers }) → createDataChannel / addTrack → createOffer → setLocalDescription → send via signaling.
  • Trap: 100-person mesh = 99 uploads each. Big calls use an SFU (Selective Forwarding Unit): upload once, server forwards.

title: The showdown
text: Audio/video/peer data → WebRTC . 2. Client sends often, low latency (chat, games, cursors) → WebSockets . Server pushes, client listens (scores, notifications, AI answers) → SSE . 4. Rare updates / delay OK → polling (long polling if faster). SSE: one-way, built-in reconnect, text, plain HTTP. WS: two-way, binary, DIY reconnect, leaves HTTP after upgrade. Polling: most compatible, most wasteful. Trap: "chat needs WebSockets" → not necessarily: SSE down + POST up is valid and stays plain HTTP (caching, auth, load balancing).
html:
1. Audio/video/peer data → WebRTC. 2. Client sends often, low latency (chat, games, cursors) → WebSockets.
  2. Server pushes, client listens (scores, notifications, AI answers) → SSE. 4. Rare updates / delay OK → polling (long polling if faster).
  3. SSE: one-way, built-in reconnect, text, plain HTTP. WS: two-way, binary, DIY reconnect, leaves HTTP after upgrade. Polling: most compatible, most wasteful.
  4. Trap: "chat needs WebSockets" → not necessarily: SSE down + POST up is valid and stays plain HTTP (caching, auth, load balancing).

title: Heartbeats
text: A dead TCP connection doesn't announce itself (sleep, Wi-Fi drop) → half-open connection; app shows "online" forever. Proxies also kill idle connections. App-level ping/pong: every message resets a timer; silence > interval + margin (e.g. 35 s for 30 s pings) → ws.close() → reconnect. Browsers answer protocol ping frames silently, and JS can't send them → apps send their own {type:'ping'} . Trap: interval must be under the shortest idle timeout on the path (often 20–30 s), but not so fast it drains batteries.
html:

  • Browsers answer protocol ping frames silently, and JS can't send them → apps send their own {type:'ping'}.
  • Trap: interval must be under the shortest idle timeout on the path (often 20–30 s), but not so fast it drains batteries.

title: Reconnect
text: See it: WhatsApp Web, Wi-Fi off → "Computer not connected" banner; on → missed messages appear. Naive instant reconnect → thundering herd after a server restart. Fix: exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8 … cap 30 s) + random jitter (S5E14). On open: resync since=<last seq> , then flush the outbox. Listen to online / offline / visibilitychange . AbortController (S5E13): one abort() removes the old socket's listeners and cancels its catch-up fetch. Trap: don't retry every close. 1000 = normal close; auth failures need re-login, not retries. Retry network errors (1006).

title: Ordering
text: One socket = TCP order. Many paths (devices, reconnects, HTTP + socket) = no order guarantee. Sender clocks lie. Server assigns a sequence number per chat . Client: drop seq <= last , buffer gaps and fetch missing ranges, apply in order. Trap: async onmessage handler that awaits (decrypt) can finish message 2 before 1 → queue and process one at a time.

title: Acks & dedup
text: WhatsApp ticks: 1 grey = server got it, 2 grey = delivered to the device, 2 blue = read. Clock = pending (optimistic UI, S4E15). Lost ack → retry → duplicate. Fix: client-generated id ( crypto.randomUUID() ), outbox until acked, server drops repeat ids, client merges its own echo. Guarantee: at-least-once + dedup ≈ exactly-once. Trap: generate the id on the client : a server id doesn't exist until the first attempt succeeds.

  • Guarantee: at-least-once + dedup ≈ exactly-once.

title: Scaling WebSockets
text: Sockets are stateful: Alice on server A, Bob on server B. Fix: pub/sub (Redis, Kafka, NATS): A publishes to user:bob , B is subscribed and pushes down Bob's socket. Keep socket servers dumb, scale out; load balancer must support Upgrade + long idle timeouts. Deploys drop every socket on a server → drain gradually, clients reconnect with jitter. Trap: sticky sessions only route reconnects to the same server; they don't deliver cross-server messages.

  • Trap: sticky sessions only route reconnects to the same server; they don't deliver cross-server messages.

title: Presence
text: Online/offline from connections + heartbeats + TTL ( SET presence:riya online EX 60 , renewed by each heartbeat). Count connections, not users (laptop closed, phone open = online). Debounce offline to avoid flapping. Fan-out: only to users currently viewing; throttle "typing…" (~1 event / 3 s, auto-expires). Trap: don't store presence in the main database → in-memory store with TTLs.

title: Edit conflicts
text: See it: Google Docs with a friend: coloured named cursors in the same sentence. Whole-document saves = last save wins → lost words. Send operations ( insert 'h' @1 ) instead. Positions shift: "cat" + insert h@1 → "chat"; concurrent delete @2 applied blindly → "cht". Adjusted to delete @3 → "cha". Forms: optimistic concurrency → PUT with If-Match: <etag> → 412 = conflict, merge or ask. Trap: locking works and users hate it (forgotten tab blocks everyone). Locks for forms/tickets, not live text.

title: OT vs CRDT
text: OT : central server orders ops and transforms late ones against earlier ones. Lean docs, needs a server. CRDT : every character gets a permanent unique id; inserts reference ids; merges in any order, peer-to-peer and offline. Costs metadata + tombstones. See it: Google Docs offline mode → edit → reconnect → merged. Trap: don't write your own. Use Yjs or Automerge ; spend time on presence, cursors, undo.
